title: Chemical and topographical 3D surface profiling using atmospheric pressure LDI and MALDI MS imaging
protocol: Fix sample on MALDI target holder with superglue.
Perform 3D optical microscopy of the sample.
Dissolve DHB and CHCA matrices in a 1:1 (v/v) acetone/water mixture containing 0.1% TFA to create matrix solutions.
Apply 100 µl of matrix solution using a pneumatic sprayer system with a flow rate of 10 µl/min and gas pressure of 1 bar.
Check matrix layer quality, crystal size, and homogeneous coverage with an optical microscope.
Calibrate mass spectrometer with known DHB cluster signals.
Mount MALDI target with sample on the target support of the modified AP-SMALDI10 MSI source.
Search region of interest in the optical sample observation camera.
Set mass range of m/z 100-1000 and fixed injection time of 500 ms for the mass spectrometer.
Apply a voltage of 4 kV to the MALDI target with respect to the MS inlet.
Set laser settings to 30 laser pulses per spot (pixel) with a repetition rate of 60 Hz.
Set step size (lateral resolution) and corresponding pixel number in the control software for measuring the entire region of interest.
Adjust laser pulse energy to desired lateral resolution.
Set lock mass in the mass spectrometer to calibrate spectra to known matrix cluster peaks.
Start mass spectrometer data acquisition and initialize the 3D scan in the control software.
Load mass spectrometric data and 3D imaging data into MIRION or MATLAB software.
Set image bin width to m/z ±0.01.
Export all relevant images with their corresponding intensity-weighted centroid m/z value as .jpg and .csv files.
Use 3D imaging data to display sample topography in a heat map color scale using MATLAB scripts.
Combine three different ion images into an RGB overlay image and integrate it with the topographic information into 3D RGB MS surface images.
Normalize MS images to the base pixel (highest intensity) per image (m/z bin).
Import m/z value list (.csv file) into METLIN database within a search window of 2 ppm for accurate mass compound assignment.
